original_question: Does the QRCP algorithm typically used in practice satisfy the above, or a similar, bound.
target_in_paper: Section 4.1.2 (Orthogonal rows), Problem 4.3: whether the practical QRCP algorithm, applied to Q^T for Q ∈ R^{n×k} with orthonormal columns, satisfies the preceding bound ||(Q(I,:))^{-1}||_2 ≤ √(k(n-k+1)) or a comparable bound.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the specific algorithm under discussion—QR with column pivoting (QRCP) as used in practice—and that the issue is whether it satisfies a theoretical bound stated immediately beforehand.
missing_details: The matrix class is missing: the subsection fixes Q ∈ R^{n×k} with k < n and orthonormal columns.
The algorithm is applied to Q^T, not to an arbitrary matrix.
The selected object is an index set I ⊂ {1,…,n} of size k, corresponding to the first k pivot columns of Q^T, equivalently k selected rows of Q.
The exact bound referred to by 'the above' is ||(Q(I,:))^{-1}||_2 ≤ √(k(n-k+1)).
The notation Q(I,:) and the fact that this is a k×k submatrix whose inverse is being bounded are implicit in the draft and need to be spelled out.
The paper's question is in the orthogonal-rows / RRQR setting, not the broader CSSP or general low-rank approximation setting.
The relevant quantifier is not average-case over inputs: the phrase 'typically used in practice' modifies the algorithm, not the input distribution.
The intended comparison for 'a similar bound' is a comparably strong non-exponential bound; the nearby context notes that existing upper bounds for QRCP grow exponentially in k.
The ambient field is real in the subsection's setup.
refined_question: Let Q ∈ R^{n×k} with k < n and Q^TQ = I_k. Apply the standard QR factorization with column pivoting (QRCP) to Q^T, and let I ⊂ {1,…,n}, |I| = k, be the indices corresponding to the first k pivot columns of Q^T (equivalently, the k selected rows of Q). It is known that there exists an index set I for which ||(Q(I,:))^{-1}||_2 ≤ √(k(n-k+1)). Does the QRCP algorithm used in practice itself always return an index set I satisfying this bound, or at least a comparably strong non-exponential bound on ||(Q(I,:))^{-1}||_2, for every such Q?
justification: The draft is essentially a shorthand for Problem 4.3 itself: the paper asks, almost verbatim, whether the practical QRCP algorithm satisfies 'the above, or a similar, bound.' The phrase 'the above' points to the immediately preceding statement in Section 4.1.2, which gives the existence bound ||(Q(I,:))^{-1}||_2 ≤ √(k(n-k+1)) for some row index set I when Q has orthonormal columns. The same subsection frames the problem as computing an RRQR of Q^T in the orthogonal-rows setting, so a faithful rewrite must unpack Q, I, the role of Q^T, and the exact norm bound, while not broadening the question beyond Problem 4.3.
